\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that someone approved, objected or argued, and talk about consensus and controversy.}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{وافق} (wāfaqa)}{وافق (wāfaqa)}]{\ar{وافق} (wāfaqa) — to approve; to agree to}

\label{lesson:AR-C360-wafaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to suggest, then the Arabic for convincing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{وافق}}
\textbf{\ar{وافق}} — \emph{wāfaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to approve; to agree to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وافق} \ar{المدير} \ar{على} \ar{الخطة} \ar{الجديدة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{wāfaqa al-mudīr ʿalā al-khiṭṭa al-jadīda.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager approved the new plan.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يوافق}, \emph{yuwāfiq}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{وافق} \ar{على} …. \ar{اتفق} is two sides agreeing with each other.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{وافق}} (\emph{wāfaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-f-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to fit, to suit\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form III, to be in accord with: to agree to a thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wāfaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wāfaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wāfaqa al-mudīr ʿalā al-khiṭṭa al-jadīda.} — The manager approved the new plan.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to suggest, then the Arabic for convincing, then say \emph{wāfaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{وافق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To approve; to agree to\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اعترض} (iʿtaraḍa)}{اعترض (iʿtaraḍa)}]{\ar{اعترض} (iʿtaraḍa) — to object}

\label{lesson:AR-C360-itarada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for convincing, then the Arabic for to approve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اعترض}}
\textbf{\ar{اعترض}} — \emph{iʿtaraḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to object\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اعترض} \ar{جارنا} \ar{على} \ar{الموسيقى} \ar{العالية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iʿtaraḍa jārunā ʿalā al-mūsīqā al-ʿāliya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our neighbour objected to the loud music.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يعترض}, \emph{yaʿtariḍ}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{اعترض} \ar{على} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اعترض}} (\emph{iʿtaraḍa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-r-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be broad; to lie across\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, to put oneself across the way: to object.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtaraḍa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtaraḍa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtaraḍa jārunā ʿalā al-mūsīqā al-ʿāliya.} — Our neighbour objected to the loud music.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for convincing, then the Arabic for to approve, then say \emph{iʿtaraḍa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{اعترض} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To object\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إجماع} (ijmāʿ)}{إجماع (ijmāʿ)}]{\ar{إجماع} (ijmāʿ) — consensus}

\label{lesson:AR-C360-ijma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to approve, then the Arabic for to object.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إجماع}}
\textbf{\ar{إجماع}} — \emph{ijmāʿ} — \textquotedblleft{}consensus\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وصل} \ar{الفريق} \ar{إلى} \ar{إجماع} \ar{بعد} \ar{نقاش} \ar{طويل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waṣala al-farīq ilā ijmāʿ baʿda niqāsh ṭawīl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The team reached a consensus after a long discussion.
\end{quote}

\ar{بالإجماع}, \emph{bi-l-ijmāʿ}, unanimously.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إجماع}} (\emph{ijmāʿ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-m-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to gather, to bring together\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ijmāʿ} is the Form IV verbal noun, a bringing together: everyone gathered on one view.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ijmāʿ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ijmāʿ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waṣala al-farīq ilā ijmāʿ baʿda niqāsh ṭawīl.} — The team reached a consensus after a long discussion.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to approve, then the Arabic for to object, then say \emph{ijmāʿ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{إجماع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Consensus\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جادل} (jādala)}{جادل (jādala)}]{\ar{جادل} (jādala) — to argue}

\label{lesson:AR-C360-jadala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to object, then the Arabic for consensus.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جادل}}
\textbf{\ar{جادل}} — \emph{jādala} — \textquotedblleft{}to argue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{جادل} \ar{الولد} \ar{أمه} \ar{حول} \ar{وقت} \ar{النوم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jādala al-walad ummahu ḥawla waqt an-nawm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boy argued with his mother about bedtime.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يجادل}, \emph{yujādil}.

You argue with someone directly, with no preposition: \ar{جادله}, argued with him.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جادل}} (\emph{jādala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-d-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to twist firmly\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form III, to twist against someone: to argue with him.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jādala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jādala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jādala al-walad ummahu ḥawla waqt an-nawm.} — The boy argued with his mother about bedtime.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to object, then the Arabic for consensus, then say \emph{jādala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{جادل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To argue\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جدل} (jadal)}{جدل (jadal)}]{\ar{جدل} (jadal) — a controversy}

\label{lesson:AR-C360-jadal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for consensus, then the Arabic for to argue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جدل}}
\textbf{\ar{جدل}} — \emph{jadal} — \textquotedblleft{}a controversy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{هناك} \ar{جدل} \ar{كبير} \ar{حول} \ar{الفيلم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna hunāka jadal kabīr ḥawla al-film.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a big controversy about the film.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جدل}} (\emph{jadal}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-d-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to twist firmly\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Jadal} is a verbal noun of the same root: arguing, and so a controversy.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jadal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jadal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna hunāka jadal kabīr ḥawla al-film.} — There was a big controversy about the film.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for consensus, then the Arabic for to argue, then say \emph{jadal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{جدل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A controversy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
